CVE-2026-53914 is unsafe deserialization of untrusted Kotlin build-cache metadata, allowing code execution (fixed in Kotlin 2.4.20). It requires local access, high privileges and high attack complexity (CVSS 6.7; the scanner inflates it to CRITICAL). The org.jetbrains.kotlin:* artifacts (compiler, scripting, build-tools, stdlib, reflect, abi-tools, etc.) are pulled by the Kotlin Gradle plugin at build time only and are not on any deployed runtime classpath. The Kotlin version is dictated by the Kotlin Gradle plugin, so it cannot be bumped per recipe module; re-evaluate when the toolchain moves to 2.4.20+. As of 2026-08-03 Maven Central has only 2.4.20-Beta2, so no fixed release is available yet. Added: 2026-07-03

CVE-2026-49844 (MODERATE, CVSS 5.9) is improper encoding of non-finite IEEE 754 values (NaN / Infinity / -Infinity) by MapMessage.asJson(), which emits bare tokens that RFC 8259 does not permit. It is reachable only when the application uses the JsonTemplateLayout message resolver (or another layout calling MapMessage.asJson()) AND logs a MapMessage holding an attacker-controlled floating-point value. Neither holds here: log4j-api / log4j-core 2.17.1 arrive build-time only, transitively via the Scala/sbt build toolchain (org.scala-sbt:zinc_2.13 -> org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-core), and are not on any deployed runtime classpath; no JsonTemplateLayout is configured and no MapMessage is logged. Patched in 2.25.5, but the version is dictated by zinc. Added: 2026-07-29

False positive. Dependency-check mines vendor evidence from the Full-Change git SHA that this plugin writes into every jar manifest. Where that 40-char hex string happens to contain "ada" it yields a LOW-confidence cpe:/a:ada:ada match — e.g. rewrite-spring-6.36.0-SNAPSHOT.jar carries Full-Change=ea9cfba8b47f090ada56cdf0dbe226ce5d6399bc, flagged for CVE-2024-9410, a blind SSRF in Ada.cx's hosted Sentry configuration. Ada.cx is a SaaS product with no Java artifact, so nothing on an OpenRewrite or Moderne classpath can ever be affected. Scoped to our own coordinates rather than one artifact because the match follows the commit SHA, not the library: roughly 1% of SHAs contain "ada", so it resurfaces on a different jar each time it recurs. Suppressed indefinitely — the CPE is mis-attributed at the source and can never become a true positive for us. Added: 2026-07-29

file name: prism-parser-api-0.0.4.jar, prism-parser-wasm-0.0.4.jar sev: CRITICAL reason: False positive. These are the Java bindings for ruby/prism, a standalone Ruby *parser* library, published under groupId org.ruby-lang. Dependency-check derives cpe:2.3:a:ruby-lang:ruby:0.0.4 from that groupId alone, and because 0.0.4 sorts below every real CRuby release (1.8.x-3.x) it numerically matches the "<= X" range of every CRuby interpreter advisory ever published — ~38 CVEs from 2008 to 2023 covering WEBrick, Net::FTP, RDoc, Rake, cgi, Fiddle/dl, OpenSSL hostname verification and the bundled oniguruma regex engine. None of that code ships here: prism-parser-api contains only org/ruby_lang/prism/Nodes*.class AST types, and prism-parser-wasm contains only the Prism parser compiled to wasm (org/ruby_lang/prism/wasm/PrismParser.*.native plus the generated PrismParserMachine* classes); `strings` over every native blob finds zero occurrences of onig/webrick/net-ftp/rdoc. Both jars arrive transitively via org.openrewrite:rewrite-ruby, which uses Prism to parse Ruby sources into an LST. Suppressed by CPE rather than per-CVE, and indefinitely: the ruby-lang:ruby product match against a parser binding is mis-attributed at the source and can never become a true positive, and a per-CVE list would need re-extending on every future CRuby advisory. Scope of this rule, since a bare <cpe> element looks broad: it is an *identifier* correction, not a vulnerability mute. CpeSuppressionAnalyzer runs at POST_IDENTIFIER_ANALYSIS and only removes the bogus cpe:/a:ruby-lang:ruby identifier from these two jars, before the NVD lookup derives any CVE from it; with no <cve> element the rule never removes a Vulnerability. Purl-based matching is therefore untouched — a genuine advisory published against pkg:maven/org.ruby-lang/prism-parser-* still surfaces (there are none today). Bounded to the 0.x line, which is exactly the range where the "sorts below every CRuby release" premise holds: if these bindings ever re-version to track CRuby, the rule stops applying and the classification gets re-examined rather than silently carried over. Added: 2026-08-17
